question.text: The Normans were led at Hastings by this man, who became King of England afterwards and commissioned the Domesday Book.
question.answerHtml: William the Conqueror [or William I; or William the Bastard; or William II of Normandy; accept Guillaume in place of William; prompt on William]
question.clue: This king ordered for a destructive campaign to gain control of Northumbria in his Harrying of the North, and he ordered for the compilation of a written record of England, the Domesday Book.

swap.leadin: A common rhyme about this figure's most famous action instructs listeners to "Remember, remember, the 5th of November."
swap.text: Name this man who conspired to blow up the British Parliament in the Gunpowder Plot. His failure to do so is commemorated in the U.K. with fireworks displays and large bonfires.
swap.clue: After the discovery of the Monteagle letter, this man was arrested and tortured for information about his fellow conspirators.

question.leadin: This leader crushed the Scots in the Battle of Worcester, a victory which caused Charles II to flee to France.
question.text: Name this Lord Protector of the England, who participated in the English Civil War.
question.clue: This victor at the Battle of Naseby would later brutally re-conquer Ireland, and this leader who fought for the "Good Old Cause" commanded the cavalry of the New Model Army during one war.

swap.leadin: Answer the following questions about World War I.
swap.text: This biggest naval battle of World War I saw Sir John Jellicoe lead the British to a tactical victory over Germany and deliver a crushing blow to any hopes of Germany gaining naval superiority over the Allies.
swap.clue: The ironically named (+) Invincible was sunk during this battle, which included a phase called the Run to the South.

question.leadin: This conflict saw the sinking of the General Belgrano by the submarine Conqueror.
question.text: Name this war that saw the Battles of Goose Green and San Carlos, as well as the sinking of the HMS Sheffield. This war was fought over a territory one of the belligerents refers to as Las Islas Malvinas.
question.clue: This conflict began when one side's troops landed on April 2, and ended when they were forced to give up the territorial capital of Port Stanley in mid-June of the same year.

swap.text: Both Walpole and Churchill also held this economic position during their careers, which sets the inflationary target for British banks and spending limits for ministerial departments.
swap.clue: Before becoming Prime Minister, Disraeli served under Lord Derby in this position, which is the highest within the Treasury of the United Kingdom.

question.leadin: William Pitt the Younger served as Chancellor of the Exchequer during the reign of a monarch from this house.
question.text: Identify this house that ruled England after the House of Stuart, producing William IV and several kings named George, like George III.
question.clue: A member of this house, the "Sailor King," oversaw the abolishment of slavery and expanded suffrage with the Great Reform Bill of 1832.

swap.text: This British wartime Prime Minister came to power after the 1916 fall of Henry Herbert Asquith. He also led the creation of the British welfare state and oversaw the Partition of Ireland in 1920.
swap.clue: After the Shell Crisis, this man was placed in charge of the newly created Ministry of Munitions.

question.leadin: The first Anglo-Saxon king to convert to Christianity, Ethelbert, ruled from a kingdom that shares its name with this county.
question.text: Identify this English county where Jack Cade's revolt against Henry VI began. The head of the Anglican Church, the Archbishop of Canterbury, rules from within this county.
question.clue: Tyler's revolt broke out in Essex and this coastal region east of Sussex. Jack Cade and Thomas Wyatt also rebelled in this region, where Augustine of Canterbury converted a king named Aethelbert.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Britain's relations with India, per part.
swap.text: The Supreme Allied Commander of Southeast Asia during World War II, he oversaw the transfer of power from Britain to India and Pakistan as the last viceroy.
swap.clue: This man's wife Edwina carried out an affair with Jawaharlal Nehru, who rejected this man's proposal for an Indian flag with a spinning wheel in place of a chakra.

question.leadin: Answer the following about John Bull, the national personification of Great Britain.
question.text: An actual person named John Bull is a composer sometimes credited with writing this British national anthem, whose title changes depending on if the monarch is male or female.
question.answerHtml: "God Save the King" [or "God Save the Queen"]

swap.leadin: They were famous for wearing blue bonnets.
swap.text: Name this political movement whose Risings aimed to restore James II to the throne of Britain.
swap.clue: The song "Hey, Johnnie Cope, are Ye Waking Yet?" made fun of a general who lost to this group at Prestonpans during a war in which their figurehead escaped to the Isle of Skye dressed as a woman.

question.text: A disciple of Columba named Aidan founded a monastery on this "holy" island off the coast of Northumbria. This island, where a namesake Gospel book was illustrated, suffered the first major Viking raid against Britain in 793.
question.clue: This place's most famous landmark was founded by Saint Aidan in 634.

swap.leadin: Bagpipe playing and kilt wearing were banned under the Act of Proscription, which was passed shortly after this last battle fought on British soil.
swap.text: Name this 1746 battle at the namesake moor that ended the Jacobite uprising and saw English forces quickly defeat approximately twelve thousand Highlanders under Bonnie Prince Charlie.
swap.clue: The battle itself lasted little more than one hour, after which the victorious army marched to Inverness and continued the slaughter.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about rampant crime in Glasgow in the 20th century.
question.text: These turf wars pitted Thomas Campbell against the Marchetti brothers and resulted in Campbell's arrest for the murder of "Fat Boy" Doyle. Its name comes from the vehicles used by Campbell to sell drugs.

swap.leadin: This person's life is attested to in part by four separate wills made from 1394 to 1416, and The Book of Margery Kempe describes a visit regarding their revelations.
swap.text: Name this fourteenth-century anchoress and author of the Showings.
swap.answerHtml: Julian of Norwich [or Juliana of Norwich; accept Lady Juliana, Dame Juliana or Mother Juliana; prompt on Julian or Juliana alone]

question.leadin: He was first elected as an MP for Northampton in 1880, but he wasn't seated until 1886, when he at last consented to take the parliamentary oath.
question.text: Name this notorious English politician, an atheist who edited the socialist publication The National Reformer.
question.clue: This author of a birth-control pamphlet and associate of Annie Besant was elected to Parliament in 1885, but his refusal to take the religious oath of Parliament led to a five-year-long scandal in the House of Commons.

swap.leadin: Identify these British Prime Ministers FTPE.
swap.text: This man became PM after the resignation of Peel. This Whig helped pass the 1847 Factory Act and 1848 Public Health Act, and repealed the Navigation Acts in 1849. His policies during the Crimean War forced him to lose office to Palmerston.
swap.clue: This man's first Prime Ministership saw the establishment of a 10-hour work day as well as a national board of public health, and he left politics for four years because of a disagreement over foreign policy and war conduct.

question.leadin: Answer the following about primary sources from the exploration and settlement of Canada.
question.text: Accounts from the expeditions of John Davis, Humphrey Gilbert, and Martin Frobisher, among others, were included in this anthologist's The Principall Navigations Voiages and Discoveries of the English Nation.
question.clue: This writer of The Principal Navigations, Voyages, and Discoveries of the English Nations first translated Grotius's Mare Liberum into English. He names a London-based society that publishes primary accounts of historic maritime voyages.

swap.leadin: This figure's wife, Margaret of France, possibly had an affair with William Marshall, who was his tournament manager and mentor.
swap.text: Name this man, who rallied the support of the counts of Flanders, Boulogne, and Blois during the Revolt of 1173, but became a celebrity for attending a bunch of tournaments with his retinue of knights. He died while fighting a campaign against his father.
